summary: GRASP relies on SMILES sequence order (position embeddings) rather than pure graph topology, ignores stereochemistry entirely, and uses coarse-grained aromaticity tokens.

claims.claim: SMILES order sensitivity is real due to absolute position embeddings.
claims.test: RDKit: Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True) vs canonical; expect distance > 0.1 if sensitive.
claims.prediction: If position_biased_input=True, distance should be ~0.14 (supervisor hint) or higher (observed 0.528).

claims.test: RDKit: Compare enantiomers (e.g., C[C@H](N)O vs C[C@@H](N)O); expect distance ~0.
claims.prediction: Distance should be 0 if stereo info is not in input tokens or model ignores it.

claims.claim: Pretrained weights encode chemical structure; random does not.
claims.test: Compare pretrained CLS vs random-init CLS on same molecules; expect low similarity.
claims.prediction: Similarity near 0 indicates orthogonal representations (learned vs noise).

claims.claim: Pretrained model learns layer-specific activation scales.
claims.test: Compute per-layer norm of A.atom[l] for pretrained; expect variation.
claims.prediction: Norms should vary by layer if model learns depth-wise features.

claims.claim: Random-init model has uniform high activation norms.
claims.test: Compute per-layer norm of A.atom[l] for random; expect constant value.
claims.prediction: Norms should be constant if random init + LayerNorm without learned scaling.

claims.claim: Aromaticity is mostly encoded as a hard class in tokens.
claims.test: Group df['aromatic'] by A.tokens; count distinct values per token.
claims.prediction: Most tokens should have only 1 aromatic value (0 or 1).

claims.claim: Pretrained model is more expressive than random.
claims.test: Compute participation ratio of covariance matrix; expect higher for pretrained.
claims.prediction: Higher rank indicates more dimensions used to capture chemical variance.

trivial_explanations: SMILES sensitivity is explained by position_biased_input=True (absolute position embeddings).
Stereo blindness is explained by lack of stereo info in input tokens or model architecture.
Token mixing fraction is explained by coarse-grained tokenization (likely element/ring status only).
Norm differences are explained by learned scaling vs random init.
